reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with nearly identical structure and correct core explanations. B adds slightly more practical depth: it shows how to check the JVM flags actually applied, gives a heap-to-limit rule of thumb, covers native/malloc growth (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX), and says which kubelet metric to watch after the change. A's mention of heap-leak diagnosis via a heap dump partly offsets this.

A: Claims requests == limits means the pod will not land on an overloaded node; equal memory requests/limits mainly affect QoS/eviction, and without CPU limits the pod is not Guaranteed QoS anyway.
B: Claims requests == limits keeps the pod from being evicted first, but its snippet sets a CPU request without a CPU limit, so the pod is Burstable rather than Guaranteed QoS.
